Conversation Practice - grammar, vocabulary, pronunciation, and more! 

Increase your fluency. 
Improve your pronunciation. 
Overcome your fear of speaking. 
Develop your listening comprehension. 
Refine your grammar. 
Expand your vocabulary. 
Enjoy a relaxed and engaging conversation. 

Do you understand English better than you speak it? If so, you're not alone. One of the most common frustrations of even the most advanced English students is that they understand what they read and hear, but struggle to express themselves in spoken exchanges. Why? The answer is simple: language learners have more opportunities to read and listen to the language they’re learning than to speak or write it. However, the only way to improve your speaking skills is through practice, ideally with a native speaker. This is especially true of English, because fluency in English depends to a great degree on its peculiar patterns of stress and intonation.

In these lessons, you will get the practice you need to increase your fluency and reach your other English-related goals. We will get to know one another in a relaxed conversation about ourselves and about topics that interest you. I will provide prompts to help you if you’re not sure what you feel like talking about during the lesson. I will also provide constructive feedback and guidance, based on areas in which you have the most room for improvement. At the end of the lesson, you will have access to a feedback document that contains my notes on any errors you made and ways you can improve. This document can serve as a guide for the practice and study you do on your own, outside of lessons.

pro_course_detail.title: Private Book Club
pro_course_detail.description:
This is a class that I created for my more advanced students that are looking to climb the mountain that is C2 proficiency. That does not necessarily mean that you need to be C1 to take this class; I will be the one that determines if you're ready for it.

In this class we will cycle through books that I'm currently reading that range from classic literature to psychology to philosophy to history to religion to science fiction and beyond. 

I will extract certain portions of the book that I'm currently on that I find to be relevant to vocabulary acquisition, obscure grammar, phrasal verbs, and prepositional phrases. I will go over these grammar points, but I will also formulate conversation topics based on the text. The student may do the same, formulating his own conversation topics, questions about vocabulary and grammar. That being said, it is not an expectation of the student to do that. 

Lastly, there are no time constraints. If a student was unable to read the chapter(s) before the next class, that is perfectly fine. We can find an alternative activity and then return to that section later on. As I am continuously reading, the classes have already been outlined most of the time and they are only fortified by each student who asks different questions. 

All new vocabulary and grammar points will be given to the student on a google slide document after the class. If the student does not have access to Google, an alternative can be arranged. 

Note: We will read the entirety of the book, BUT there is no expectation or time constraint on the student. 

Current book: Homo Deus. Author: Yuval Noah Harari

pro_course_detail.description:
It is no secret that one of the best ways to improve foreign language skills is to read in them as much as possible. In fact, our knowledge of languages can perhaps best be measured in the kilometers of text we’ve read in them!

Literature provides access to a treasure trove of language, which we can use to enrich our own speech, writing and understanding. It provides the absolute best examples of careful and precise language usage, from which we can learn more than any English textbook.

At the same time, reading in a foreign language allows us to discover and explore new worlds. But instead of traveling through space, we travel through text! Reading is, perhaps, the best way to deepen our understanding of other cultures. The universe of literature written in English or translated into this language is boundless, and your journey though it can provide lifelong enjoyment!  

As a teacher of literature, I can help you make reading in English interesting and fun!

pro_course_detail.title: Conversation and Reading for Kids
pro_course_detail.description:
Children have a natural curiosity but a short attention span—especially when learning a new language! That’s why this English lesson is packed with visual, interactive elements designed to keep kids engaged and having fun. 

Through games, songs, and dynamic activities, children pick up English in a way that feels more like play than study. The focus is on conversation, so they quickly build confidence speaking in real-life scenarios, from greeting others to expressing their ideas. 

As soon as they reach a basic level of fluency, we also introduce early reading to further support their progress. By nurturing a love for language at an early age, our program helps children grow into enthusiastic, fluent English speakers, ready to connect with the world around them. 

With a child-centered approach, they’ll be excited to join every lesson, and parents will be thrilled with their progress!
